newsitem.title: POLAND: IB Austria sees Poland's KGHM 1997 net up 59.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: IB Austria sees Poland's KGHM 1997 net up 59.5 pct.

text.p: The net profit of Poland's KGHM copper concern, to be floated in Warsaw and London on July 10, is likely to rise 59.5 percent this year against 1996, IB Austria Securities Research in Warsaw said on Tuesday.
It said in a report that according to conservative estimates KGHM's net profit would rise to 330.7 million zlotys this year and to 352.5 million zlotys in 1998.
"If current trends in copper prices and zloty exchange rate hold, KGHM's net profit this year may be even 20 percent higher than our estimate," the IB Austria report said.
It said it expected revenue from sales to rise 12.8 percent to 3.98 billion zlotys this year and to 4.18 billion zlotys in 1998.
The report stressed that KGHM's financial results depended mainly on the prices of copper on world markets and could only partly be improved by the company's cost cutting programme.
The production of one tonne of copper in 1996 cost KGHM $1,952 but the firm said it wanted to cut it down top $1,450 per tonne in the year 2000.
"Taking into account the (strategy of cost cutting), the cost structure in competing firms and the report of mining engineers, we think reaching that target is unlikely," the IB Austria report said.
"We expect KGHM will eventually cut total production costs to $1,650-$1,600 per tonne," the report said.

IB Austria said it valued the company at 4.5 billion zlotys. It said it had arrived at the figure by discounting expected future profits, evaluating KGHM's interests in areas outside of its mining business and applying market ratios similar to that of other leading copper firms.
The public offering price range of 18-23 zlotys priced the whole firm at 3.6-4.6 billion zlotys.
